title: Je voudrais
subtitle: Polite “I would like”
explanation: Use je voudrais to ask for something politely or to say what you would like to do.

examples.eng: I would like a room for two people for two nights, please.
examples.fre: Je voudrais une chambre pour deux personnes pour deux nuits, s'il vous plaît.

examples.eng: I would like to go to the restaurant.

title: Prendre
subtitle: Taking or having food and drink
explanation: Prendre means “to take,” and in this course it is also used naturally for having food or drink.

title: Puis-je / pouvoir
subtitle: Asking “can I?” or “may I?”
explanation: Use puis-je before a verb to ask politely if you can or may do something.

examples.eng: Can I have a room for tonight?
examples.fre: Puis-je avoir une chambre pour ce soir?

examples.eng: Can I pay for the wine?
Can I go to the bank?

title: Avez-vous / avoir
subtitle: Asking “do you have?”
explanation: Use avez-vous to ask whether someone has something. It is a useful polite question in hotels, restaurants, and shops.

examples.eng: Do you have a table for four people?
examples.fre: Avez-vous une table pour quatre personnes?

examples.eng: Do you have a map of the city?
examples.fre: Avez-vous un plan de la ville?

title: Partitive articles: du, de la, des
subtitle: Saying some / any
explanation: Use du, de la, or des when talking about an unspecified amount or number of something, such as some cheese, coffee, or apples.

title: C'est / ce n'est pas
subtitle: Saying it is / it is not
explanation: Use c'est for “it is” or “this is.” Use ce n'est pas to make the same idea negative.

title: Definite and indefinite articles
subtitle: Using the / a / an
explanation: French nouns commonly use articles such as le, la, les for “the” and un, une, des for “a,” “an,” or plural “some.”

title: Avec / sans
subtitle: With and without
explanation: Use avec for “with” and sans for “without.” These are useful when asking for rooms, food, or other options.

examples.eng: Can I have a room with a balcony?
examples.fre: Puis-je avoir une chambre avec un balcon?

examples.eng: Can I have a pizza but without the cheese?
examples.fre: Puis-je prendre une pizza mais sans le fromage?

examples.eng: May I have two coffees without sugar?
examples.fre: Puis-je prendre deux cafés sans sucre?

title: Chez
subtitle: At someone’s place
explanation: Use chez before a person to mean “at” or “to” that person’s home or place.

examples.eng: I would like to go to Lucie's house.
Can I go to George's house?

title: À / au / aux
subtitle: Going to and being at places
explanation: Use à with places. It combines with le to make au and with les to make aux.

examples.eng: I would like to go to the restaurant.
I would like to go to the toilet.

title: Où est / où sont
subtitle: Asking where something is
explanation: Use où est for one thing or person and où sont for more than one.

title: Pour aller à...?
subtitle: Asking how to get somewhere
explanation: The course uses pour aller à...? as a practical way to ask how to get to a place.

examples.eng: How do I get to Paris?
How do I get to the restaurant?
How do I get to the city centre?

title: Direction commands
subtitle: Allez, prenez, tournez
explanation: Use allez, prenez, and tournez when giving directions: go, take, and turn.

title: Location and direction phrases
subtitle: Left, right, straight on
explanation: Use à gauche, à droite, and tout droit to describe where something is or which way to go.

examples.eng: The hotel is on the right.

title: Ordinal forms
subtitle: First, second, third
explanation: Première, deuxième, and troisième are used with roads and exits to say first, second, and third.

title: Puis / et puis
subtitle: Saying then / and then
explanation: Use puis or et puis to put actions in sequence, especially when giving multi-step directions.

examples.eng: Go straight on and then turn left.
examples.fre: Allez tout droit et puis tournez à gauche.

examples.eng: Take the third road on the left and then turn right.
examples.fre: Prenez la troisième rue à gauche et puis tournez à droite.

examples.eng: Take the second road on the right and then go straight on.
examples.fre: Prenez la deuxième rue à droite et puis allez tout droit.

title: Vers
subtitle: Saying towards
explanation: Use vers to show the direction you are moving or turning toward.

title: Avant / après
subtitle: Before and after
explanation: Use avant for “before” and après for “after” to place an action before or after another place, event, or time.

examples.fre: Tournez à gauche avant le rond-point.
Tournez à gauche après le rond-point.

examples.eng: I would like to go to the beach after lunch.
examples.fre: Je voudrais aller à la plage après le déjeuner.

title: Trop
subtitle: Saying too / too much
explanation: Use trop to say something is too much or has too much of a quality.

title: Plus / moins
subtitle: More, less, bigger, smaller
explanation: Use plus to compare with “more” and moins for “less.” With adjectives, they create ideas such as bigger or smaller.

title: Un peu and quantity with de
subtitle: A bit / a little
explanation: Use un peu for “a bit.” Before a noun, use un peu de, and the course also combines quantity expressions with plus de and moins de.

examples.eng: I would like a bit of cheese.
examples.fre: Je voudrais un peu de fromage.

examples.eng: I would like a bit more cheese.
examples.fre: Je voudrais un peu plus de fromage.

title: Adjective agreement
subtitle: Matching adjectives to nouns
explanation: French adjectives can change to match the noun. The course shows changes such as grand/grande and plural forms such as grandes.

title: Demonstrative adjectives: ce, cet, cette, ces
subtitle: Saying this / that / these
explanation: Use ce, cet, cette, or ces before a noun to point out “this,” “that,” or “these,” depending on the noun.

title: Colours and adjective placement
subtitle: Describing colour
explanation: Colour words usually come after the noun in these course examples, and some change form to agree with the noun.

examples.eng: I would like the red coat.

title: Ça / cela
subtitle: Saying that
explanation: Use ça or cela to refer to “that.” The course uses both forms in practical requests and descriptions.

title: Aimer / préférer
subtitle: Saying what you like or prefer
explanation: Use j'aime to say “I like” and je préfère to say “I prefer.” They can be joined to compare choices.

examples.eng: I like the green coat but I prefer the red coat.
examples.fre: J'aime le manteau vert mais je préfère le manteau rouge.

title: Direct object pronouns: le, la, l’
subtitle: Replacing “it”
explanation: Use le, la, or l' before the verb to replace a thing already mentioned. This avoids repeating the noun.

examples.eng: I would like it in wood.

title: En + colour or material
subtitle: Saying in red / in wood
explanation: Use en before a colour or material to describe the version or material you want, like en rouge or en bois.

examples.eng: I would like it in wood.

title: Stressed pronouns: moi, lui, elle
subtitle: For me, him, her
explanation: Use moi, lui, and elle after words such as pour to say “for me,” “for him,” or “for her.”

examples.eng: A bit more for him, please.
examples.fre: Un peu plus pour lui, s'il vous plaît.
Un thé pour elle, s'il vous plaît.

title: Time expressions
subtitle: Telling and asking the time
explanation: Use à quelle heure to ask “at what time.” The course also practices heures, et demie, et quart, and moins le quart.

examples.fre: À quelle heure est le petit-déjeuner demain?
Il est dix heures et demie.
C'est à six heures moins le quart.

title: Par
subtitle: Per day / month / person
explanation: Use par to express a rate such as per day, per month, or per person.

examples.eng: The car is twenty euros per day.
examples.fre: La voiture est vingt euros par jour.

title: Ticket forms and plurals
subtitle: One-way and return tickets
explanation: The course uses un aller simple for a one-way ticket and un aller-retour for a return ticket. Their plural forms change when talking about several tickets.

title: Infinitives after helper expressions
subtitle: Combining verbs
explanation: After expressions such as je voudrais or puis-je, another verb often stays in the infinitive, as in payer, faire, or aller.

examples.eng: I would like to pay for the wine, please.
examples.fre: Je voudrais payer le vin, s'il vous plaît.

examples.eng: I would like to go at three o'clock.
examples.fre: Je voudrais aller à trois heures.

title: Negation: ne...pas
subtitle: Making sentences negative
explanation: Put ne before the verb and pas after it to say something is not true or does not happen.

examples.eng: It isn't for her; it's for me.
examples.fre: Ce n'est pas pour elle; c'est pour moi.

title: Numbers and quantities
subtitle: Counting people, tickets, and prices
explanation: The course uses numbers with nouns, prices, times, and quantities. Keep the noun plural when the quantity requires it.

examples.eng: How much is it for three tickets?
The car is twenty euros per day.
examples.fre: La voiture est vingt euros par jour.
